cues: On the veranda, Veena props him up on pillows that make his head swim: Rakesh says you can sit if you try.
He stares at the gate, which carries his son's name and degrees; his own name vanished long ago.
The doctor arrives in white with a new tonic and reaches out, ever devoted, to press his father's feet.
The old man tucks them away, and with one grand sweep knocks the bottle from his son's hand.
Brown syrup stains the white trousers.
For once there is noise and attention around him, and he lies back like a prophet and groans that God is calling him: now let him go.
